RFC-MA.verify_note: Shape = average of the 3 digitized RFC-8MA/-13MA/-20MA log-log Impedance-vs-frequency curves (label-anchored calibration: 0.01MHz-100MHz decade lines, 117px/dec; 1000ohm top, 155px/dec). Same family behaviour as MRFC: inductive rise to a broad peak ~1-3MHz (norm ~1.35), fall through 10MHz (=1.0) to a dip ~30MHz (0.79), then a second rise toward the 100MHz edge (1.36). VERIFY-BACK: digitized raw Z@10MHz per part = 42.9/35.9/34.6 ohm (avg ~38). Published spot 'Impedance >=20 ohm/10MHz(1turn)' is a GUARANTEED MINIMUM, graph is 'measured data for reference, not guaranteed'; digitized ~38 ohm sits above the >=20 guarantee (typical~2x guaranteed-min), so consistent. z_spot_ohm=20 copied exactly from '>= 20'. RFC-13MA cable spec is a RANGE phi12.5-13.5mm -> cable_max_mm=13.5. NOTE: chart x-axis ends at 100MHz (data traces to ~125MHz); the 300MHz point is EXTRAPOLATED from the rising second-hump tail (~2x/decade) and is uncertain.

RFC-A.verify_note: Shape digitized from the per-part log-log Impedance-vs-frequency graphs (median of RFC-6-A, RFC-8-A, RFC-9-A, RFC-13-A). Red curves start ~5-11 ohm at 1 MHz and end at ~490-506 MHz (they do NOT extend to 1000 MHz), so the 1000 MHz point is a mild extrapolation anchored on the real ~500 MHz reading (norm ~1.9) plus a quadratic log-log fit (~1.5); 1.8 used as a near-plateau value. Verify-back at 100 MHz: digitized absolute Z(100MHz) = RFC-6-A:217, -8-A:186, -9-A:183, -13-A:214 ohm vs published minima (>=135,120,125,123). Digitized runs consistently ~1.47-1.74x the published '>=N' (all outside a strict +/-25% band). The graphs plot typical measured data while the table gives the guaranteed floor, so digitized exceeding the '>=' minimum by ~50-75% is expected; the consistency validates the digitization and the z_spot_ohm field keeps the published catalog minima verbatim.

KTFC.verify_note: 1-turn (blue) curve digitized from log-log graph; frame calibrated f=1..1000 MHz, Z=10..10000 ohm. Raw Z: 1MHz=14, 3=31, 10=57, 30=75, 100=104, 300=244 ohm. Curve terminates ~490 MHz so no 1000 MHz reading (null, not invented). Verify-back: digitized ~104 ohm at 100 MHz sits on the 100-ohm gridline; published is a guaranteed minimum >=66 ohm, so measured-typical exceeding it (+58%) is expected for a >= spec, not a calibration error.

GTFC.verify_note: Shape averaged from pixel-digitization of 5 clearest log-log curves (16-8-13, 16-8-16, 20-10-10, 23-11-14, 25-15-12); y-axis calibrated to decade gridlines (1000@px3083..1@px3495), x-axis f=1 at left frame + 141.3px/decade. Plotted curves only extend to ~500 MHz, so the 100 MHz point is well-supported but the 1000 MHz normalized value (2.5) is an EXTRAPOLATION of the flattening HF tail (norm~2.0 at the 500 MHz curve end), not read from the graph. Verify-back: digitized 100 MHz absolute Z per part: 16-8-13=78, 16-8-16=96, 20-10-10=67, 23-11-14=97, 25-15-12=65 ohm vs published minima 45/55/40/55/40 -> a consistent ~1.6-1.8x (avg 1.7x). This exceeds +-25% but is EXPECTED: the catalog column is a guaranteed MINIMUM (>=N) while the curves are reference-measured typicals (page note: 'measured data for reference, not guaranteed'). Ratios are consistent across all parts, confirming the readings track the published floor.

KRFC.verify_note: Shape = 1-turn (blue) curve, digitized by color+log-log calibration from 4 clear plots (KRFC-6/8/10/13); normalized shapes agree within a few percent through 300 MHz. Blue 1-turn trace ends ~500 MHz (still rising, ~2.4x the 100 MHz value); the 1000 MHz point (2.6) is a modest extrapolation beyond the measured data. Verify-back: digitized 1-turn absolute value at 100 MHz reads ~127-187 ohm across parts vs the published guaranteed-minimum spots of 70-120 ohm, i.e. the reference-measured curves run ~55-65% ABOVE the table spot (outside +/-25%). This is expected: table spots are guaranteed minimums (>=) while the graph is 'measured data for reference, not guaranteed' (typical), a ~1.6x guard band. Normalized shape is robust regardless of this absolute offset.

GTFCK.verify_note: GTFCK.pdf contains NO impedance-vs-frequency graphs (only the parts table); it is the chassis-mount (M4 screw) variant of GTFC using the IDENTICAL toroidal ferrite cores - same core designations (16-8-13 ... 41-27-16), same applicable cable diameters, and same published Z minima (45/55/40/55/40/50/70/50 ohm at 100 MHz). The normalized shape is therefore INHERITED from the GTFC catalog graphs (same cores). Shape averaged from pixel-digitization of 5 clearest GTFC log-log curves; curves plot only to ~500 MHz so the 1000 MHz normalized value (2.5) is an extrapolation of the flattening HF tail, not read. Verify-back cross-checks the GTFC curves' digitized 100 MHz Z (78/96/67/97/65 ohm) against these same published minima -> consistent ~1.7x, expected because >=N is a guaranteed floor vs reference-measured typicals.

GTFCR.verify_note: GTFCR.pdf is a single page with only the parts table and mechanical profiles; it contains NO impedance-vs-frequency graph, so no curve could be digitized (shape_norm100 left empty, per the same convention as sibling GRFC/RFC-A data files). Parts table verified verbatim: GTFCR-16-8-16 Max.phi7.2mm, >=55 ohm; GTFCR-41-27-16 Max.phi26mm, >=50 ohm at 100MHz/1turn. Both rows match the reference kitagawa_tables.json exactly.

RFCW.verify_note: shape_norm100 = RFCW-C10 (high-frequency, spec'd at 100 MHz) red curve, digitized by color+log-log calibration. The two RFCW parts have DIFFERENT shapes: C10 is a smooth monotonic rise (high-freq sleeve clamp); RFCW-13MA is a low-cut resonant shape (rises to a ~2 MHz peak ~1.4x, dips to a ~30 MHz min ~0.8x, rises again toward 100 MHz) captured in shape_13ma_norm10 (normalized at its 10 MHz spec freq; its x-axis spans 0.1-100 MHz only). Verify-back: C10 red at 100 MHz digitizes to ~222 ohm vs published >=140 (ratio 1.59); 13MA red at 10 MHz digitizes to ~34 ohm vs published >=20 (ratio 1.7). Both run ~55-70% ABOVE the table spot (outside +/-25%) for the same reason as KRFC: table spots are guaranteed minimums (>=) while the graphs are 'measured data for reference, not guaranteed' (typical) -- a ~1.6x guard band. C10 red trace ends ~500 MHz at ~1.9x the 100 MHz value; the 1000 MHz shape point (2.3) is a modest extrapolation beyond the measured data. Normalized shapes are robust regardless of the absolute offset.

GRFC.verify_note: Shape digitized from the per-part log-log Impedance-vs-frequency graphs (median of the 6 standard Profile-1 parts: GRFC-5,6,8,9,10,13). Red curves start near 10 ohm at 1 MHz and end at ~490-506 MHz (they do NOT extend to 1000 MHz), so the 1000 MHz point is a mild extrapolation anchored on the real ~500 MHz reading (norm ~2.5) plus a quadratic log-log fit (~2.1); 2.4 used as a near-plateau value. Verify-back at 100 MHz: digitized absolute Z(100MHz) = GRFC-5:138, -6:133, -8:102, -9:99, -10:147, -13:130, -7:55 ohm vs published minima (>=100,100,75,75,105,95,45). Digitized runs consistently ~1.33-1.40x the published '>=N' (GRFC-7 is +23%, within +/-25%; the rest ~+33 to +40%). The graphs plot typical measured data while the table gives the guaranteed floor, so digitized exceeding the '>=' minimum by a consistent ~35% is expected and confirms the digitization tracks the family; the z_spot_ohm field keeps the published catalog minima verbatim.

MRFC.verify_note: Shape = average of the 3 digitized MRFC-8/-13/-20 log-log Impedance-vs-frequency curves (label-anchored calibration: 0.01MHz-100MHz decade lines, 117px/dec; 1000ohm top, 155px/dec). Curves: inductive rise (slope +1) to a broad peak ~1-3MHz (norm ~1.3), fall through 10MHz (=1.0) to a dip ~30MHz (0.78), then a second rise toward the 100MHz edge (1.33). VERIFY-BACK: digitized raw Z@10MHz per part = 50.9/35.6/34.8 ohm (avg ~40). Published spot 'Impedance >=20 ohm/10MHz(1turn)' is a GUARANTEED MINIMUM, while graph is 'measured data for reference, not guaranteed'; digitized ~40 ohm is comfortably above the >=20 guarantee (typical~2x guaranteed-min), so consistent. z_spot_ohm=20 copied exactly from '>= 20'. NOTE: chart x-axis ends at 100MHz (data traces to ~125MHz); the 300MHz point is EXTRAPOLATED from the rising second-hump tail (~2x/decade) and is uncertain.

BFCWN.verify_note: Each part has its own single red 1-turn curve; all 4 frames pixel-calibrated (Z=1..1000 ohm, 71.33 px/decade; MA-NC x=0.01..100 MHz, A-BK x=1..1000 MHz). Raw digitized Z at spec freq: 2010MA-NC=39.7 ohm @1MHz (pub >=20), 2010-A-BK=181 ohm @100MHz (pub >=117), 3515MA-NC=30.6 ohm @1MHz (pub >=16), 3515-A-BK=181 ohm @100MHz (pub >=117). Digitized-vs-published: measured curve runs ~1.5-2x above the published spot in every case, consistent because the published values are GUARANTEED MINIMUMS (>=), while the graph is 'measured data for reference, not guaranteed' (typical exceeds min). Direction and shape verified visually. MA-NC curves are the low-cut double-hump (peak ~1MHz, dip ~10-30MHz, rise to 100MHz) and do not extend past 100 MHz. A-BK curves terminate near ~500 MHz, so no 1000 MHz reading (null, not invented).

BCN.verify_note: Block core, ferrite core inside a nylon-66 clamp; treated as solidRing thread-through. cable_max_mm = E, the larger (long) inner-window dimension the flat cable passes through (short dim B~2.0mm). z_spot values read directly from the parts table. NOTE: the BCN impedance-graph x-axis prints its leftmost tick as '0.01' but the confirmed one-decade-per-77px minor-gridline pattern proves the four decade lines are consecutive (10,100,1000 self-consistent), so the axis is 1-10-100-1000 MHz and '0.01' is a datasheet misprint for '1'; this reading also matches the published 100MHz spot. Shape digitized from the BCN-26 graph. Curve ends ~490MHz so 1000MHz=null. Verify-back: digitized 100MHz=202ohm vs published spot >=125ohm -> ratio 1.62 (measured curve above guaranteed-minimum spec).

BREK.verify_note: 1-turn (blue) curve digitized from BREK-45-60-20 graph (clean 4-decade log-log calibration). Digitized 1 MHz = 36.4 ohm vs published spot >=20 ohm; ratio 1.82. Published spot is a guaranteed MINIMUM (>=), typical measured curve running ~1.8x above the floor. Shape near-identical to BRE (same nanocrystalline material), monotonic 0.48 (0.1MHz) -> 2.58 (100MHz).

BRE.verify_note: 1-turn (blue) curve digitized from BRE-16-25-10 graph (clean 4-decade log-log calibration). Digitized 1 MHz = 45.8 ohm vs published spot >=28 ohm; ratio 1.64. The published spot is a guaranteed MINIMUM (>=), so typical measured curve running ~1.6x above the floor is expected/consistent. Shape rises monotonically 0.44 (0.1MHz) -> 2.63 (100MHz).

GFPC.verify_note: Spots read directly from parts-table Impedance column (guaranteed >= at 100MHz), not the graph. Shape digitized from GFPC-16-8-2 graph (representative mid-range curve; all 18 graphs share the same soft-ferrite log-log rise). Digitized Z(100MHz) ~ 45 ohm vs published spot >= 25 for that part; ratio ~1.8 (graph is typical reference data above the guaranteed minimum, expected). Curve ends ~600 MHz so 1000 MHz = null.

GFPH.verify_note: Single graph (GFPH-10-6-5). Digitized Z(100MHz) ~ 40 ohm vs published spot >= 25; ratio ~1.6 (graph is typical reference data above the guaranteed minimum, expected). Curve ends ~550 MHz so 1000 MHz = null.

GFPO.verify_note: Shape digitized from GFPO-25-12-3 graph (all 3 graphs share the same soft-ferrite log-log rise). Digitized Z(100MHz) ~ 55 ohm vs published spot >= 35 for that part; ratio ~1.6 (graph is typical reference data above the guaranteed minimum, expected). Curve ends ~550 MHz so 1000 MHz = null.

GRIB.verify_note: Single published curve digitized; matches GRI ferrite-bead shape. Verify-back: digitized 100MHz=111 ohm vs published >= 75 (ratio 1.48, consistent with GRI small cores). Curve ends ~500 MHz so 1000MHz=null. GRIB is a 2-hole rib core; cable threads the phi-D hole so cable_max_mm = D = 1.5 (per-hole diameter).

GRIP.verify_note: NO impedance spot column in the catalog table; z_spot_ohm=32 was READ from the graph at 100 MHz (digitized 31.6 ohm), not published. Verify-back N/A (no published spot to compare). Shape is a near-straight rising log-log line (inductive, Z proportional to f), distinct from the GRI/GRIB bead plateau. cable_max_mm=1.6 = MAX of the cylindrical lead outer diameter range phi0.6-1.6 (grips a discrete-device lead; also rectangular leads 0.8-1.5W x 0.3-0.7T). Curve ends ~500 MHz so 1000MHz=null.

GRI.verify_note: Shape is the average of 8 digitized part curves (normalization cancels absolute offset; per-point SD<=0.04 except 300MHz SD=0.15 from varying end upturn). y-axis calibration verified: decade lines at 155 px/decade. Curves end ~500 MHz so 1000MHz=null. Verify-back: digitized 100MHz sits ~1.3-1.5x above the conservative published >= spot; e.g. GRI-11-25-5 digitized 152 vs spot 105 (1.44), GRI-14-28-6 187 vs 130 (1.44); larger 16/17.5 cores lower ~1.16-1.21.

GSSC.verify_note: cable_max_mm = E, the larger (long) opening dimension of the flat through-slot (short dim B~1.3-2.2mm). All 10 z_spot values read directly from the parts table (not the graph). Shape digitized from the GSSC-33.5-8 impedance graph (all 10 curves near-identical straight log-log lines). Curve ends ~490MHz so 1000MHz=null. Verify-back: digitized 100MHz=43.5ohm vs published spot >=30ohm -> ratio 1.45 (measured curve above guaranteed-minimum spec).

GSSH.verify_note: cable_max_mm = E, the larger (long) opening dimension of the flat through-slot (short dim B~1.2mm). Shape digitized from the GSSH-33.5-12 impedance graph (all 4 curves near-identical straight log-log lines). Curve ends ~490MHz so 1000MHz=null. Verify-back: digitized 100MHz=50.7ohm vs published spot >=35ohm -> ratio 1.45 (measured curve above guaranteed-minimum spec).

GTRCA.verify_note: Round toroidal core with PA66 housing, non-split. cable_max_mm = actual inner-hole phi B (8.2 / 12.8), smaller than nominal in the part name due to the housing. Spots read from the parts table (>=45 / >=40). 1-turn (red) curve of GTRCA-20-10-10 digitized. At 100 MHz ~62 ohm vs published spot >=45 ohm, ratio ~1.38 (reference measured data exceeds guaranteed min). Curve ends ~600 MHz -> 1000 MHz null.

GTRE.verify_note: Oval (elliptical) toroidal core, non-split. Inner opening C(inner height)=10.0 x D(inner width)=4.0 mm; max round cable limited by narrow dim D=4.0 mm. 1-turn (red) curve of GTRE-14-12.5-8 digitized. At 100 MHz ~40 ohm vs published spot >=30 ohm, ratio ~1.33 (reference measured data exceeds guaranteed min). Curve ends ~500 MHz -> 1000 MHz null.

GTR.verify_note: Shape = mean of 3 digitized curves (GTR-40-27-15, GTR-28-16-20, GTR-16-8-16), monotonic rising log-log, normalized to 1.0 at 100MHz. 1000MHz=null: all measured curves terminate ~500-600MHz (never reach 1GHz gridline), not extrapolated. Verify-back at 100MHz vs published guaranteed minimum: GTR-40-27-15 ~70 vs >=45 (1.56x), GTR-28-16-20 ~95 vs >=70 (1.36x), GTR-16-8-16 ~102 vs >=65 (1.57x); typicals run 1.36-1.57x the >=N floor, within the expected 1.3-2x band. Note per catalog these graph values are reference measured data, not guaranteed.

KTR.verify_note: 1-turn (blue) curve of KTR-25-15-18E digitized. At 100 MHz ~72 ohm vs published spot >=54 ohm, ratio ~1.33 (graph is reference measured data, exceeds guaranteed minimum -- consistent). Blue curve ends ~550 MHz, so 1000 MHz null.

MPTR.verify_note: SPEC IS 5-TURN (not 1-turn like BRE/BREK): catalog header 'Impedance* Ohm/1MHz (5turn)'. Single red curve digitized from MPTR-40-24-15E graph (clean 4-decade log-log). Digitized 1 MHz = 25.2 ohm vs published spot >=12 ohm; ratio 2.1 (spot is guaranteed MINIMUM). Metal-powder core => INDUCTIVE shape (Z ~ proportional to f, slope ~1) rising from 0.11 (0.1MHz) to a broad peak, still climbing to 32x by 100MHz -- fundamentally steeper than the lossy nanocrystalline BRE/BREK. Curve starts ~0.037MHz, continuous to 100MHz (no nulls). All 3 MPTR graphs share this shape; z-spot ratios differ slightly (7,12,12 floors).

TRCB.verify_note: DEVIATION: TRCB is a Mn-Zn soft-ferrite LOW-frequency cased toroid, non-split; its published spot is at 10 MHz (table header 'Impedance Ohm/10MHz (1 turn)'), NOT 100 MHz like KTR/GTRE/GTRCA. Graph x-axis spans 0.01-100 MHz. Shape is normalized at 10 MHz (the spec frequency) so Z(f)=z_spot*shape is self-consistent -- key is shape_norm10, not shape_norm100. Characteristic double-hump: peak ~32 ohm near 2 MHz, dip ~19 ohm near 25-30 MHz, rising again to ~52 ohm at 100 MHz. cable_max_mm = inner phi B (8.1/13.3/16.6). 1-turn (red) curve of TRCB-19-10-10 digitized. Verify-back at 10 MHz: digitized ~22 ohm vs published spot >=11 ohm, ratio ~2.0 (reference measured data well above the conservative guaranteed minimum). Curve ends ~130 MHz -> 300 & 1000 MHz null.

TRMH.verify_note: Shape = per-part MEDIAN of the digitized 1-turn (blue) |Z|(f) curve across all 11 TRMH panels, normalized to 1.0 at the 1 MHz spec freq. Curve rises to a first peak near 0.5-1 MHz, dips to ~0.77 through 3-30 MHz, then rises strongly toward 100 MHz. The 100 MHz upturn is STRONGLY size-dependent: small cores norm~1.1-1.5, large high-mu cores (65/74/103/160) norm~7-55 (second dimensional resonance), so median 1.51 represents the typical/smaller cores. Axis ends at 100 MHz so 300 MHz = null. VERIFY-BACK: digitized 1-turn value at 1 MHz vs published spot per part ratio = [1.66,2.37,2.29,2.67,3.81,3.01,2.58,2.71,2.77,2.82,2.45], median 2.67. Graph reads ~2.7x the table spot because the table gives GUARANTEED MINIMUMS (>=) while graphs are typical reference measured data (not guaranteed). Note: graph panel labels the TRMH-27 part 'TRMH-27-19-16' but the parts table (used here) says TRMH-27-19-15.

TRM.verify_note: Shape = per-part MEDIAN of the digitized 2-turn (orange) |Z|(f) curve across all 7 TRM panels, normalized to 1.0 at the 10 MHz spec freq. Curve rises from ~0.05 MHz, peaks ~1-2 MHz (norm~1.4-1.6 vs 10 MHz), dips to ~0.73 near 30 MHz, then rises back toward 100 MHz (norm~1.0, size-dependent range 0.6-1.7). Axis ends at 100 MHz so 300 MHz = null. VERIFY-BACK: digitized 2-turn value at 10 MHz vs published spot per part ratio = [1.81,2.23,3.18,2.17,2.48,2.23,2.88], median 2.23. Graph reads ~2.2x the table spot because the catalog table gives GUARANTEED MINIMUMS (>=) while the graphs are typical reference measured data (not guaranteed), per the catalog footnote.
